   301→class SQLLineageHolder(ColumnLineageMixin):
   302→    def __init__(self, graph: DiGraph):
   303→        """
   304→        The combined lineage result in representation of Directed Acyclic Graph.
   305→
   306→        :param graph: the Directed Acyclic Graph holding all the combined lineage result.
   307→        """
   308→        self.graph = graph
   309→        self._selfloop_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SELFLOOP)
   310→        self._sourceonly_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SOURCE_ONLY)
   311→        self._targetonly_tables = self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.TARGET_ONLY)
   312→
   313→    @property
   314→    def table_lineage_graph(self) -> DiGraph:
   315→        """
   316→        The table level DiGraph held by SQLLineageHolder
   317→        """
   318→        table_nodes = [n for n in self.graph.nodes if isinstance(n, DATASET_CLASSES)]
   319→        return self.graph.subgraph(table_nodes)
   320→
   321→    @property
   322→    def column_lineage_graph(self) -> DiGraph:
   323→        """
   324→        The column level DiGraph held by SQLLineageHolder
   325→        """
   326→        column_nodes = [n for n in self.graph.nodes if isinstance(n, Column)]
   327→        return self.graph.subgraph(column_nodes)
   328→
   329→    @property
   330→    def source_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   331→        """
   332→        a list of source :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   333→        """
   334→        source_tables = {
   335→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg == 0
   336→        }.intersection(
   337→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg > 0}
   338→        )
   339→        source_tables |= self._selfloop_tables
   340→        source_tables |= self._sourceonly_tables
   341→        return source_tables
   342→
   343→    @property
   344→    def target_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   345→        """
   346→        a list of target :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   347→        """
   348→        target_tables = {
   349→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg == 0
   350→        }.intersection(
   351→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg > 0}
   352→        )
   353→        target_tables |= self._selfloop_tables
   354→        target_tables |= self._targetonly_tables
   355→        return target_tables
   356→
   357→    @property
   358→    def intermediate_tables(self) -> Set[Table]:
   359→        """
   360→        a list of intermediate :class:`sqllineage.core.models.Table`
   361→        """

   363→            table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.in_degree if deg > 0
   364→        }.intersection(
   365→            {table for table, deg in self.table_lineage_graph.out_degree if deg > 0}
   366→        )
   367→        intermediate_tables -= self.__retrieve_tag_tables(NodeTag.SELFLOOP)
   368→        return intermediate_tables
   369→
   370→    def __retrieve_tag_tables(self, tag) -> Set[Union[Path, Table]]:
   371→        return {
   372→            table
   373→            for table, attr in self.graph.nodes(data=True)
   374→            if attr.get(tag) is True and isinstance(table, DATASET_CLASSES)
   375→        }

   377→    @staticmethod
   378→    def _build_digraph(
   379→        metadata_provider: MetaDataProvider, *args: StatementLineageHolder
   380→    ) -> DiGraph:
   381→        g = DiGraph()
   382→        for holder in args:
   383→            g = nx.compose(g, holder.graph)
   384→            if holder.drop:
   385→                for table in holder.drop:
   386→                    if g.has_node(table) and g.degree[table] == 0:
   387→                        g.remove_node(table)
   388→            elif holder.rename:
   389→                for table_old, table_new in holder.rename:
   390→                    g = nx.relabel_nodes(g, {table_old: table_new})
   391→                    g.remove_edge(table_new, table_new)
   392→                    if g.degree[table_new] == 0:
   393→                        g.remove_node(table_new)
   394→            else:
   395→                read, write = holder.read, holder.write
   396→                if len(read) > 0 and len(write) == 0:
   397→                    # source only table comes from SELECT statement
   398→                    nx.set_node_attributes(
   399→                        g, {table: True for table in read}, NodeTag.SOURCE_ONLY
   400→                    )
   401→                elif len(read) == 0 and len(write) > 0:
   402→                    # target only table comes from case like: 1) INSERT/UPDATE constant values; 2) CREATE TABLE
   403→                    nx.set_node_attributes(
   404→                        g, {table: True for table in write}, NodeTag.TARGET_ONLY
   405→                    )
   406→                else:
   407→                    for source, target in itertools.product(read, write):
   408→                        g.add_edge(source, target, type=EdgeType.LINEAGE)
   409→        nx.set_node_attributes(
   410→            g,
   411→            {table: True for table in {e[0] for e in nx.selfloop_edges(g)}},
   412→            NodeTag.SELFLOOP,
   413→        )
   414→        # find all the columns that we can't assign accurately to a parent table (with multiple parent candidates)
   415→        unresolved_cols = [
   416→            (s, t)
   417→            for s, t in g.edges
   418→            if isinstance(s, Column) and len(s.parent_candidates) > 1
   419→        ]
   420→        for unresolved_col, tgt_col in unresolved_cols:
   421→            # check if there's only one parent candidate contains the column with same name
   422→            src_cols = []
   423→            # check if source column exists in graph (either from subquery or from table created in prev statement)
   424→            for parent in unresolved_col.parent_candidates:
   425→                src_col = Column(unresolved_col.raw_name)
   426→                src_col.parent = parent
   427→                if g.has_edge(parent, src_col):
   428→                    src_cols.append(src_col)
   429→            # if not in graph, check if defined in table schema by metadata service
   430→            if len(src_cols) == 0 and bool(metadata_provider):
   431→                for parent in unresolved_col.parent_candidates:
   432→                    if (
   433→                        isinstance(parent, Table)
   434→                        and str(parent.schema) != Schema.unknown
   435→                    ):
   436→                        columns = metadata_provider.get_table_columns(parent)
   437→                        for src_col in columns:
   438→                            if unresolved_col.raw_name == src_col.raw_name:
   439→                                src_cols.append(src_col)
   440→
   441→            # Multiple sources is a correct case for JOIN with USING
   442→            # It incorrect for JOIN with ON, but sql without specifying an alias in this case will be invalid
   443→            for src_col in src_cols:
   444→                g.add_edge(src_col, tgt_col, type=EdgeType.LINEAGE)
   445→            if len(src_cols) > 0:
   446→                # only delete unresolved column when it's resolved
   447→                g.remove_edge(unresolved_col, tgt_col)
   448→
   449→        # when unresolved column got resolved, it will be orphan node, and we can remove it
   450→        for node in [n for n, deg in g.degree if deg == 0]:
   451→            if isinstance(node, Column) and len(node.parent_candidates) > 1:
   452→                g.remove_node(node)
   453→        return g
   454→
   455→    @staticmethod
   456→    def of(metadata_provider, *args: StatementLineageHolder) -> "SQLLineageHolder":
   457→        """
   458→        To assemble multiple :class:`sqllineage.core.holders.StatementLineageHolder` into
   459→        :class:`sqllineage.core.holders.SQLLineageHolder`
   460→        """
   461→        g = SQLLineageHolder._build_digraph(metadata_provider, *args)
   462→        return SQLLineageHolder(g)
